text:
Marie: Hey team — proposing a small reorg/addition to the GPU fleet dashboard: a Tenant Noise Aggregate panel (sparkline + 99p overlay) to surface short noisy tenants that cause thermal/power blips across racks. Thinking this will help correlate tenant bursts -> inlet temp / power throttle events.

AJ: +1 on idea. Can you sketch expected queries and thresholds? want to make sure we don't create alert churn. :eyes:

Marie: Rough draft PromQL below. Goal: per-tenant 95p/99p GPU util + sum of tenant memory allocs, then a cross-host inlet_temp mean and pdu_power. Use recording rules for 99p if possible.

Marie: ```
# tenant GPU util 99p over 5m (needs label 'tenant')
tenant_gpu_util_99p: quantile_over_time(0.99, gpu_utilization[5m]) by (tenant)

# sparkline series: weighted tenant allocs (vram bytes / gpu_count)
weighted_tenant_vram_bytes: sum by (tenant) (tenant_vram_alloc_bytes / gpu_count)

# host-level inlet temp (avg across GPUs on host)
host_inlet_temp_avg: avg by(host) (node_inlet_temp_celsius)

# PDU power per rack
rack_pdu_power: sum by(rack) (pdu_power_watts)
```

Diego: Looks good. Two suggestions: 1) use recording rule for tenant_gpu_util_99p so dashboard is cheap. 2) Add a "burstiness" score: stddev_over_time(util[10m]) / max_over_time(util[10m]) to rank noisy tenants.

Rana: For alerts, we should avoid pure 99p-based firing. Consider anomaly alert that checks: tenant_gpu_util_99p > baseline + 3*stddev AND rack_pdu_power > threshold. This reduces false positives from single-host noise.

Marie: Agreed. Example alert logic sketch:```
expr = (tenant_gpu_util_99p - tenant_gpu_util_baseline) > (3 * tenant_gpu_util_stddev)
AND on(rack) rack_pdu_power > 5000
for: 10m
labels: severity=warning, team=eng-infra
```

AJ: Can the panel show per-tenant sparkline + a small heatmap to the right that maps tenant->rack impact? That way ops can click a tenant and see which racks saw the temp/power bump.

Marie: Yes — plan: left column sparkline list (top 10 noisy tenants sorted by burstiness), right column rack heatmap overlay with inlet temp and pdu_power as color series. Clicking tenant filters heatmap using grafana variables.

Diego: UX nit: include an annotation stream for recent provisioning / maintenance windows and any capacity reshuffles (so noise from rebalancing is visible). We already push events to grafana annotations via ops-bot.

ops-bot: Deployment note: dashboard v2.6 template pushed to staging grafana at https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abC123/gpu-ops-template. Use variable tenant=~"$tenant". :rocket:

Marie: Also adding a small table below with top-5 correlated metrics per tenant (memory_pressure, cpu_steal, network_egress_bytes) to help root cause. Quick PromQL examples:```
# memory pressure pct
tenant_memory_pressure_pct: (tenant_vram_alloc_bytes / tenant_vram_capacity_bytes) * 100
# network egress rate per tenant
tenant_network_egress_bps: rate(tenant_network_egress_bytes[1m])
```

Rana: For SLO considerations, let's tag tenants that are SLA-critical. If a critical tenant spikes, page on severity=high; otherwise, create a ticket for the tenant owner. We should surface the SLA label in the panel row.

AJ: Ops question — will this be heavy on Prometheus? if we use quantile_over_time without recording rules we're going to spike query CPU.

Marie: Yes — that's why I want recording rules for the 95/99 and the burstiness score. We can compute per-tenant aggregates in a separate rules namespace to sharding-friendly labels (drop pod/instance).

Diego: Implementation plan:
- marie: PR with dashboard JSON + variable schema (tenant, rack, sla)
- diego: add recording rules in infra/rules/tenant_aggregates.yaml and test in staging rule-runner
- aj: review alerting thresholds and SLO mappings
- rana: define paging policy for SLA-critical tenants

Marie: I'll open the PR today. Panel title: "Tenant Noise Aggregate (sparkline + rack heatmap)". Will include an example screenshot and queries.

grafana-bot: New dashboard diff created: dashboard id 10234 -> changeset 6. Preview: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/10234/preview

AJ: Nice. Add a small toggle to switch smoothing windows (5m/10m/30m) — sometimes we want to see shorter microbursts.

Marie: Good call. Also adding an optoverlay: show only tenants with burstiness > 0.25 to keep list short by default.

Rana: One more: annotate region constraints. If a tenant is pinned to eu-west and we see cross-region noise, it's probably network egress causing GC on model instances. Add region dimension to heatmap.

Marie: noted. I'll include region label and test cross-region filter.

Diego: When you open the PR, link the staging dashboard and include a short checklist for oncall to validate: sample tenant, annotation sanity, recording rule doc.

Marie: Will do. Thanks all — merging plan after AJ's alert threshold review. :thumbsup:
